cards.example: The new procedure was adopted, albeit with considerable reluctance from senior staff.
cards.note: Va seguido de adjetivo, adverbio o sintagma, no de oración completa: "albeit slowly", no "albeit it was slow".

cards.back: a pesar de, no obstante (muy formal)
cards.example: Notwithstanding the budget cuts, the department met all of its targets.
cards.note: Puede ir antes o después del sustantivo: "the cuts notwithstanding". Típico de textos jurídicos.

cards.example: Poor communication between the two teams only exacerbated the delays.
cards.note: Colocaciones: exacerbate tensions / a problem / symptoms. Más formal que "make worse".

cards.example: Several measures were introduced to mitigate the impact of the floods on local businesses.
cards.note: No confundir con "militate against" (obrar en contra de). Sustantivo: mitigation.

cards.example: The region has experienced an unprecedented rise in demand for skilled workers.
cards.note: Colocaciones: unprecedented scale / levels / step.

cards.example: There are risks inherent in any attempt to automate decision-making.
cards.note: Rige "in": inherent in something.

cards.example: Auditors noticed a discrepancy between the stock records and the physical count.
cards.note: Rige "between". Para opiniones se usa más "disagreement".

cards.example: The minister's expenses came under intense public scrutiny.
cards.note: Colocaciones: come under / be subject to / withstand scrutiny.

cards.example: Constant last-minute changes undermine the team's confidence in the plan.
cards.note: Suele implicar un daño gradual o indirecto.

cards.example: A set of shared values underpins the organisation's approach to recruitment.
cards.note: Sustantivo: underpinning. No confundir con undermine (lo contrario).

cards.example: Moving the plant to a new site would entail significant retraining costs.
cards.note: Va seguido de sustantivo o -ing: "it entails working nights".

cards.example: The minor drop in sales hardly warrants a complete overhaul of the strategy.
cards.note: Formal. "Further investigation is warranted" = está justificado investigar más.

cards.example: The journalist was unable to substantiate her claims with documentary evidence.
cards.note: Lo contrario: unsubstantiated claims / allegations.

cards.example: The new rules curtail the ability of companies to export personal data.
cards.note: Colocaciones: curtail spending / powers / freedom.

cards.example: The positive results bolstered support for the reform within the party.
cards.note: Colocaciones: bolster confidence / the economy / a claim.

cards.example: Rescue efforts were hampered by heavy snow and poor visibility.
cards.note: Muy frecuente en pasiva. Sinónimo: hinder, impede.

cards.example: Additional buses were laid on to alleviate congestion during the festival.
cards.note: Colocaciones: alleviate poverty / pain / pressure.

cards.example: Mentoring schemes help foster a culture of continuous learning.
cards.note: También "foster child" (hijo de acogida).

cards.example: The success of the project hinges on securing the second round of funding.
cards.note: Implica que una sola condición es clave. También "hinge upon".

cards.example: In this case, the benefits of early intervention far outweigh the costs.
cards.note: Estructura: the advantages outweigh the drawbacks.

cards.example: A single software error rendered the entire database unusable.
cards.note: "Render something + adj." es formal; también "render assistance" (prestar ayuda).

cards.example: The study encompasses all aspects of rural development, from transport to housing.
cards.note: Más formal que "include" o "cover".

cards.example: The report fails to convey the urgency of the situation.
cards.note: Colocaciones: convey a message / an impression / meaning.

cards.example: It is difficult to discern any clear pattern in the figures.
cards.note: Adjetivo: discernible (perceptible). "Discerning" = exigente, con criterio.

cards.example: The plan presupposes that interest rates will remain low.
cards.note: Sustantivo: presupposition.

cards.example: It can be hard to reconcile economic growth with environmental protection.
cards.note: "Reconcile X with Y". También: cuadrar cuentas (reconcile accounts).

cards.example: Investigators are trying to ascertain the cause of the outage.
cards.note: Muy formal; equivale a "find out".

cards.example: A larger share of the budget has been allocated to staff training.
cards.note: Sustantivo: allocation. Colocación: allocate resources / funds.

cards.example: The team compiled a list of all suppliers that had failed inspections.
cards.note: También compilar código en informática.

cards.example: The building was deemed unsafe and evacuated immediately.
cards.note: Sin "as": "deemed necessary", no "deemed as necessary" (aunque se oye, se considera menos correcto).

cards.example: The company issued a statement refuting the allegations of negligence.
cards.note: Estrictamente significa demostrar que algo es falso; "deny" solo es negarlo.

cards.example: The accident prompted a review of safety procedures across the sector.
cards.note: Estructura: prompt somebody to do something.

cards.example: The survey yielded some surprising results.
cards.note: Sustantivo: yield (rendimiento). "Yield to" = ceder el paso / ceder ante.

cards.example: The 2015 guidelines have now been superseded by a revised edition.
cards.note: Ortografía: con "s", no "supercede".

cards.example: All contractors must adhere to the site safety rules.
cards.note: Sustantivo: adherence. Formal frente a "stick to".

cards.example: The new software enhances the accuracy of the forecasts.
cards.note: Se aplica a cualidades (calidad, reputación), no a personas.

cards.example: Without public subsidies, the scheme is not financially viable.
cards.note: Sustantivo: viability. Colocaciones: viable option / alternative.

cards.example: Residents want to see tangible improvements, not just promises.
cards.note: Lo contrario: intangible (assets).

cards.example: The inspector produced a comprehensive report on the state of the bridge.
cards.note: Falso amigo parcial: no significa "comprensivo" (= understanding).

cards.example: The wording of the contract is ambiguous and open to interpretation.
cards.note: Sustantivo: ambiguity. Diferente de "ambivalent" (con sentimientos encontrados).

cards.example: The cut-off date seemed entirely arbitrary to most applicants.
cards.note: Pronunciación: /ˈɑːbɪtrəri/.

cards.example: The government has yet to present a coherent strategy on housing.
cards.note: "Consistent" se usa para comportamiento constante; "coherent" para lógica y claridad.

cards.example: Engineers are assessing whether a tunnel is technically feasible.
cards.note: Colocación: feasibility study (estudio de viabilidad).

cards.example: There is a pervasive sense of distrust towards official statistics.
cards.note: Suele tener connotación negativa.

cards.example: The location of the new incinerator remains highly contentious.
cards.note: Sinónimo: controversial. Colocación: contentious issue.

cards.example: Long working hours can be detrimental to both health and productivity.
cards.note: Rige "to": detrimental to something.

cards.example: There was an implicit assumption that everyone would work overtime.
cards.note: Lo contrario: explicit. "Implicit trust" = confianza total.

cards.example: This type of fraud is particularly prevalent among small online retailers.
cards.note: Sustantivo: prevalence (prevalencia).

cards.back: compromiso, equilibrio entre ventajas e inconvenientes
cards.example: There is always a trade-off between speed and accuracy.
cards.note: Rige "between". Verbo: trade off X against Y.

cards.example: The whole argument rests on the premise that demand will keep growing.
cards.note: Plural "premises" también significa "local, instalaciones": on the premises.

cards.example: Share prices plummeted after the company issued a profit warning.
cards.note: Verbo intransitivo: no lleva objeto. Sinónimo: plunge.

cards.example: Energy prices soared during the winter months.
cards.note: Sinónimos: rocket, skyrocket (más informales).

cards.example: After rising steadily for five years, enrolment levelled off in 2023.
cards.note: Ortografía británica: levelled, levelling. Sinónimo: level out, plateau.

cards.example: The figures show only a marginal increase in productivity.
cards.note: Otros adjetivos: slight, negligible (insignificante), modest.

cards.example: Sales plateaued in the third quarter despite heavy advertising.
cards.note: También sustantivo: reach a plateau.

cards.example: Water consumption fluctuates considerably depending on the season.
cards.note: Sustantivo: fluctuation. "Fluctuate between X and Y".

cards.example: Unemployment peaked at 26% before starting to fall.
cards.note: "Peak at" + cifra. Sustantivo: reach a peak.

cards.example: Analysts believe the housing market has finally bottomed out.
cards.note: Implica que empezará a recuperarse.

cards.example: Visitor numbers dipped slightly in February before recovering in spring.
cards.note: Sustantivo: a dip in sales.

cards.example: Online orders surged during the lockdown.
cards.note: Sustantivo: a surge in demand. Matiz de rapidez repentina.

cards.example: The village's population has dwindled to fewer than two hundred.
cards.note: Disminución gradual hasta quedar poco.

cards.example: Wages have stagnated while living costs continue to rise.
cards.note: Connotación negativa. Sustantivo: stagnation.

cards.example: Exports rebounded strongly in the second half of the year.
cards.note: También sustantivo: a rebound in tourism.

cards.example: Demand for engineers is outstripping supply.
cards.note: Muy útil: "demand outstrips supply".

cards.example: The number of applications has more than doubled since 2019.
cards.note: "Treble" es más británico; "triple" también es correcto.

cards.example: There has been a steady rise in the number of electric vehicles on our roads.
cards.note: Otros: gradual, sustained, consistent rise.

cards.example: The chart shows a sharp drop in output in April.
cards.note: Sinónimos: steep, dramatic, sudden.

cards.example: Crime figures have followed a downward trend for over a decade.
cards.note: Lo contrario: an upward trend. "Buck the trend" = ir a contracorriente.

cards.example: Wind power accounts for roughly a quarter of total generation.
cards.note: Útil en descripción de gráficos de sectores.

cards.example: The vast majority of respondents supported the proposal.
cards.note: Concordancia: "the majority of people are..." (plural con sustantivo plural).

cards.back: una fracción de, una mínima parte de
cards.example: Solar panels now cost a fraction of what they did twenty years ago.
cards.note: "A small fraction" enfatiza lo poco.

cards.example: Losses in excess of two million euros were reported.
cards.note: Equivale a "more than" en registro formal.

cards.example: Roughly one in five households has no internet connection.
cards.note: "Roughly" es neutro; "approximately" más formal; "in the region of" también formal.

cards.example: Revenue grew by 8% year on year.
cards.note: También adjetivo: a year-on-year increase.

cards.example: The inflation rate currently stands at 3.2%.
cards.note: Para el valor actual: "stands at"; para el pasado: "stood at".

cards.example: The difference between the two groups was negligible.
cards.note: No confundir con "negligent" (negligente).

cards.front: to hit a record high / low
cards.example: Petrol prices hit a record high last summer.
cards.note: También "an all-time high".

cards.example: Complaints tapered off once the new system was in place.
cards.note: Implica reducción progresiva hacia cero.

cards.example: Rainfall in the region has become increasingly erratic.
cards.note: Para datos sin patrón claro.

cards.front: to be on the rise / on the decline
cards.example: Cybercrime is on the rise, while traditional burglary is on the decline.
cards.note: Expresiones útiles para variar frente a "increase/decrease".
